_note: Hound definitions for systems the engine already paper-trades. Edit copy freely; ids and system_id are load-bearing. rule_text for the five signal hounds is generated from the genome by src/hounds/house.py:genome_rule_text and checked by tests/test_hounds_house.py.

hounds.name: Beagle
hounds.rule_text: Bets the home team on the moneyline in every game, one unit, at the best price on the board. It uses no information at all, which is the point: it is the bar a real hound has to clear.

hounds.name: Basset
hounds.rule_text: Bets the under on the game total in every game, one unit, at the best price on the board. The direction was fixed in code before any board was read and never changes, so it is a baseline, not a pick.

hounds.name: Collie
hounds.rule_text: Bets the over on the game total in every game, one unit, at the best price on the board. Its own probability is just the market's de-vigged number republished unchanged, so it claims no opinion and no edge; it measures how good the market's own number is.

hounds.name: Pointer
hounds.rule_text: Bets the full-game moneyline, one unit, at most one bet a game, only once the lineups are posted, and only when at least 3 books are quoting it. It takes the best price on the board. It watches 3 pre-registered signals, each with its direction fixed before any results were known: (1) how heavily a starter leans on his one favourite pitch (the side facing the more predictable starter is favoured), firing at a median-sized gap between the two teams, counted double; (2) how ground-ball-heavy a starter is (the side facing the bigger ground-ball pitcher is hurt), firing at a median-sized gap between the two teams; (3) how far a starter's fastball sits above league pace (the side facing the harder thrower is hurt), firing at a median-sized gap between the two teams. Each signal that fires adds its weight to the side it points at; it bets a side once that total reaches 1 and at least 1 signal agrees. If both sides qualify the heavier side is bet, and a tie is no bet. It never uses the price to choose a side.

hounds.name: The Old Dog
hounds.tagline: Retired: the original public value card.
hounds.rule_text: Each day it published a short card of baseball bets, mostly batter props with some moneylines, ranked by how far its own model's probability sat from the market's de-vigged number, and always filled the card out to three bets with labelled fills. Paused by the owner after 2026-10-16: its picks paid a premium over the market's fair number, and its forecasts carried nothing the market did not already know (docs/decisions/MLB_VALUE_PICKS_PAUSED.md).

retired.cause: paused 2026-10-16: paid a premium over the market's fair number

hounds.verdict_sentence: The referee does not re-measure this hound: its bets are entries on the published card, not engine decisions with a stored closing board. The owner's pause cites a separate diagnosis that found closing-line value negative wherever it could be measured (docs/decisions/MLB_VALUE_PICKS_PAUSED.md).
